newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma backs gvt tax code, final vote later.
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma backs gvt tax code, final vote later.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of the Russian parliament on Thursday approved in principle a draft tax code which the cabinet says is crucial for the 1998 budget.
A total of 294 deputies voted for the resolution and only 80 against. Deputies will present amendments and then vote around 1400 GMT for the final text of the resolution.

Ministers say the new package aims to help business by simplifying the tax system and is vital to put shaky state finances in order. They say the 1998 budget would be in jeopardy unless the Duma passed it before the summer recess.
The resolution passed by the Duma said the second reading of the bill should start on November 1.
Earlier this week the government offered a compromise to the Duma, which allows deputies to present amendments to the tax code up to September after it has been approved in the first reading.

"The cabinet is ready to take into account a maximum of deputies' proposals and objections in the further discussions on the tax code," Deputy Finance Minister Sergei Shatalov said while presenting the draft code to the Duma on Thursday.
Ministers say the code will help cut domestic producers' tax burden, stabilise the tax system and decrease tax pressure on private individuals.

It suggests cutting the number of tax groups applied to Russian citizens and businesses to 28 from 75. As a result the government will lose 73-75 trillion roubles ($12.6-$13 billion), but enterprises would save money and be able to make greater investment, Shatalov said.

Private individuals will pay a 30 percent income tax on annual earnings of more than 60 million roubles and only 12 percent on anything below that level. Now Russia is using a five-grade tax system with a top rate of 35 percent.

Both government and opposition have denied rumours of a secret deal under which the Communists would back the draft while ministers would stop mentioning the possiblity of President Boris Yeltsin dissolving the legislature.
Despite the denials the Duma's Communist group, the main opposition to the government, and a number of other big factions, said they would vote for the tax code.
Only the liberal opposition Yabloko faction appeared to be opposed to the draft, while ultra-nationalists of Vladimir Zhirinovsky joined the Communists in backing it. ($ = 5760 Russian Roubles)
